claims.claim: Israel's Communications Law (Telecommunications and Broadcasting) 1982, the Anti Spam Act, prohibits advertising by automated dialing, fax or text messages without the recipient's prior opt-in consent, and requires an opt-out in every such message. claims.claim: datetime.fromisoformat only parses the full ISO-8601 range, including a trailing Z, from Python 3.11 onward, so the bundled analyzer requires Python 3.11+.

claims.claim: The benchmark thresholds this skill carries are conventional industry targets, not measured Israeli figures. Resolution rate good > 70%, average 50-70%, needs work < 50%. First contact resolution good > 65%, average 45-65%, needs work < 45%. Escalation good < 15%, average 15-30%, needs work > 30%. Abandonment good < 20%, average 20-35%, needs work > 35%. CSAT good > 4.0. Intent accuracy good > 85%, average 70-85%, needs work < 70%. Thumbs up ratio good > 80%, average 60-80%, needs work < 60%. Loop rate good < 3%, average 3-5%, needs work > 5%. NPS good > 30. Uptime target 99.9%. Statistical significance standard p < 0.05, that is 95% confidence. P95 response time means 95% of responses are faster. Trend arrows treat a change under 1% as no change, and a rate expressed as a share of a total is 100% at most. Only the fallback-rate row is externally sourced. The default alerting thresholds are operational choices set by this skill, not measured benchmarks: escalation rate above 35% in an hour, CSAT below 3.0 over two hours, abandonment rate above 40% in an hour, fallback rate above 25% in half an hour, P95 response time above 3 seconds in a quarter hour, and more than 20 new unrecognized intents in an hour. Tune them to your own traffic.
claims.raw_snippet: Rates above 20% indicate significant gaps in training or the knowledge base.
claims.verification: Only the fallback-rate benchmark has an external source (OMQ chatbot KPI lexicon: 'Benchmark: < 10%', 'Below 5% is excellent', plus the quoted sentence, read via Playwright). Every other threshold in the skill's benchmark tables is conventional practice with no measured Israeli sample behind it. The skill body now says so explicitly and instructs readers to replace each row with their own baseline after four weeks of data. Recorded at low confidence deliberately rather than dressed up with a citation that does not support it. The alerting thresholds are stated as operational defaults chosen for this skill rather than sourced benchmarks, so they are recorded here for traceability and not presented as external facts.
